streams.reasoning: From Chemistry Plan stream_logic: All reagents and solvent mixed to form homogeneous reaction mixture. Concentration matches batch (0.3 M). Flow rate derived from calculation (Step 3) to achieve target residence time.

mixing_order_reasoning: From Chemistry Plan: Reagents dissolved together in batch; co-feeding or premixing is acceptable. Single stream implies premixing or single pump feed.
pre_reactor_steps: Dissolve 4-Fluoronitrobenzene and Piperazine in DMF to 0.3 M concentration.
Filter solution (0.22 micron) to prevent clogging of narrow ID tubing.
post_reactor_steps: Quench with water (standard aqueous workup as per batch protocol).
Extract with ethyl acetate or similar organic solvent.
chemistry_notes: SnAr reaction of 4-fluoronitrobenzene with piperazine. Thermal reaction at 120 C. No photochemistry. No deoxygenation required (air tolerant). Kinetic control (Da=0.77 in calculation, but flow ensures plug flow advantage). BPR not strictly required by boiling point margin (153 C vs 120 C) but recommended for system stability and to prevent solvent evaporation at pump head if pressure drops. Calculation suggests BPR not required, but Analogy 2 used BPR for high T. We will set BPR to 0 as per calculation Step 8, but note that a low BPR (e.g. 5-10 bar) is good practice for high T DMF.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Calculation Step 2 estimated 36.0 min based on 10x intensification factor (IF) from batch 6h. Analogy 1 used 30 min at 250 C (higher T). Analogy 2 used 30 min at 220 C. Our T is 120 C (same as batch), so we rely on the calculated kinetic reduction. 36 min is within the calculated range [24.0-154.3].
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Single phase liquid system. Basis is liquid volume / liquid flow.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Same as batch (120 C). Analogy 1 and 2 used higher T (250/220 C) due to flow safety advantages, but our calculation assumes batch T to maintain yield profile unless specified otherwise. Chemistry Plan confirms 120 C.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Calculation Step 8 states BPR not required (bp DMF 153 C > 120 C + 20 C). Analogy 2 used BPR at 220 C. We follow calculation for 120 C.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA is preferred for high temperature (120 C) and chemical resistance to DMF. FEP is also acceptable but PFA has higher temp rating. Analogy 2 used Hastelloy for 220 C, but PFA is sufficient for 120 C.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.3 M from Batch Input and Chemistry Plan. Analogy 1 used 0.5 M, Analogy 3 used 1.0 M. We stick to batch concentration to ensure solubility and yield consistency.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Calculated in Step 3: V = t * Q = 36 min * 0.5 mL/min = 18.0 mL. This matches the calculated volume.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm from Calculation Step 3. Analogy 2 used 3.175 mm (larger scale). 1.0 mm provides good heat transfer and plug flow (Pe=415).
